query:
The group decided to order pizza. What did Soo-Yeon's response to that decision reveal about her actual position, and what specifically in how she responded signals this — given that she did not object?

Options:
A. Soo-Yeon
B. Nadia
C. Lena
D. Kezia
context:
[1] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:26:00) Priya mentioned pizza for tonight. Can we do something lighter? I had a heavy lunch 😅
[2] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:20:00) I'll just have Raj's flatbread.
[3] (about=Kezia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:19:00) fine with pizza 🍕
[4] (about=Priya, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:21:00) lol ok pizza it is i guess 😅 majority wins. Nadia you want in on the order?
[5] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:22:00) No. I do not eat during sessions. Order what you want.
[6] (about=Raj, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:16:00) Food situation: I brought more of those flatbreads. Can we decide before we start round two? Who's ordering and what?
[7] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:13:00) she has good taste in groups 🙂
[8] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:13:00) so basically Soo-Yeon ran a successful theory of mind intervention tbh. she identified the barrier and reframed the proposition. elegant
[9] (about=Lena, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:10:00) so basically that explains why Nadia didn't push back on Tomasz's Dune ruling even though everyone else was complaining tbh
[10] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-03-30T19:46:00) Lena's merchant tile placement in round two signaled she was building toward Coventry. Blocking Dudley removes that route. It's spatial denial, not aggression.
agent_answer:
Soo-Yeon’s response revealed she didn’t actually want pizza: although she didn’t object, she signaled her position by saying, **“I’ll just have Raj’s flatbread,”** opting out of the pizza order.

**A. Soo-Yeon**

query:
The group discussed the expectation that everyone should bring either a game or food to the annual marathon. What did Nadia's response signal about her actual relationship to this group norm, and how would you know from what she said?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Tomasz
C. Marcus
D. Lena
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:06:00) I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.
[2] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
[3] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[4] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[5] (about=Priya, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:07:00) that totally counts Nadia! honestly a good game pitch is worth more than another bag of chips 😊
[6] (about=Lena, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:10:00) so basically that explains why Nadia didn't push back on Tomasz's Dune ruling even though everyone else was complaining tbh
[7] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:38:00) I did not want to interrupt the game.
[8] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:07:00) Last April. Nadia found that I was one of the few people in the group who owned the base game for that particular series. We played four sessions over six weeks.
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:36:00) Thank you. I did not say anything but I noticed that as well.
[10] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:05:00) Yes. Everyone keep their food away from the card area please.
agent_answer:
Nadia’s response signaled that she accepts the norm only in its minimal form: she will bring a game, which satisfies the “bring a game or food” expectation, but she explicitly opts out of the food side — “I do not participate in the food arrangement.” So her actual relationship to the group norm is partial compliance with a clear boundary: she contributes the game but does not take part in the food contribution, even though Marcus framed “both” as ideal and Tomasz framed full contribution as the social contract. Priya’s reply (“that totally counts Nadia!”) confirms her game satisfies the rule.

**Answer: A. Nadia**
